ledger.purpose: Write-as-you-go OK/ERROR ledger for the five-layer security audit. Each key is written when its layer completes, so a layer that never ran leaves its key ABSENT instead of looking successful. A missing status is a FAILURE under verification check 15, never an implicit OK, and is never backfilled with a guess.
ledger.key_equivalence_note: The four *_status keys are the pre-agent set check 15 names verbatim; the six short-form keys are exactly findings-merged.json _summary.layer_status, so the merge populates all six from here with zero drift and invents nothing. Equivalent keys always carry the same value. layer_1 and layer_3b have no *_status form because check 15's *_status set covers the pre-agent layers only.
ledger.absent_key_semantics: A key absent here means that layer recorded no status; check 15 reads that as FAILURE, not as success.
ledger.write_discipline: Normative rule, not a historical claim: a layer's status key may be written only after that layer's criterion has been verified against that layer's own artifacts, the file is re-emitted after every such write, and a layer that never ran leaves its key absent rather than looking successful. Whether this run obeyed that rule is not asserted here - it is measured per layer in status_publication_events and summarised in write_discipline_conformance, which records the deviations instead of concealing them.

write_discipline_conformance.method: For each of the six layers, the criterion stated on that layer's record was re-evaluated mechanically against the artifact blobs present at every commit in the range, and the earliest commit satisfying it was compared with the earliest commit whose layer-status.json carried a status key for that layer. All times are git author timestamps in UTC and every value below is reproducible from git.
write_discipline_conformance.verdict_meaning: Every criterion is satisfied at the audited revision and every status here is correct as an end state. Three publication-order deviations occurred while the run was in progress. An earlier wording of write_discipline asserted ordered evidence-gating as a historical fact for all six layers; the measurement below contradicts that for three of them, so the assertion has been replaced by this record.

write_discipline_conformance.consumer_guidance: Read the top-level status keys as an end-state assertion about the audited revision, which is what they are and what verification check 15 tests. Do not read them as a claim about the order in which they were written while the run was in progress; for that, read status_publication_events.

status_publication_events.contract: Append-only. One record per layer, ordered by the sequence in which statuses were first published, which is the same order write_order names. Each record binds a status key to the criterion artifacts it depends on, to the commit at which that criterion was first satisfied, to the commit at which the status was first published, and to the revision at which the criterion was last re-measured.
status_publication_events.derivation_rule: The top-level status keys of this file are DERIVED from these records: a key exists if and only if its layer's record carries criterion_satisfied_at_audited_revision true, and the key's value is that record's status. A layer with no record, or with an unsatisfied criterion, carries NO key here, and verification check 15 reads that absence as failure. A status is never backfilled at merge time from the mere presence of an artifact.
status_publication_events.criterion_artifact_digests: Recorded once in provenance.attested_outputs and re-measured by security-audit/verify.sh check 15, rather than copied into each event, so there is no second copy of a digest that can drift from the first.
status_publication_events.retention_rule: This ledger is created when Layer 0 completes and is retained for the remainder of the run. It is re-emitted in place as each subsequent event is appended and is never deleted and recreated, because a deleted ledger destroys the only evidence that distinguishes a layer that succeeded from a layer that never ran. This run violated the rule once, at aa5d7633ba, which write_discipline_conformance.continuity records.
status_publication_events.status_absence_rule: A layer's status key is withheld until every artifact its criterion names exists AND the criterion evaluates true over those artifacts. Existence alone is not sufficient: at c6a86ae2f4 both Layer 1 artifacts existed while the criterion was still unmet, and at b1b24b8716 the Layer 3a status was published while two of its four artifacts did not yet exist. Neither state may produce a status key.
status_publication_events.atomicity: An event and the status key it derives are a single unit of work: the file is written whole to a temporary path in the same directory and renamed over itself, so a reader observes either the state before the event or the state after it, never a half-written ledger with an event but no key or a key but no event.

criterion_reverified_at.note: this remediation pass modifies none of the seventeen attested criterion artifacts, so the re-measurement stands for the current tree as well

events.note: criterion and status appeared in the same commit; the record was removed at aa5d7633ba and restored at b1b24b8716, which write_discipline_conformance.continuity documents

ledger.gate_contract: Any ERROR here fires the gate's ERROR branch, which outranks BLOCK, WARN and PASS in strict precedence. A layer documented ERROR here may legitimately lack its normalized findings artifact (checks 3 and 10) and contributes zero to the merged summary's expected counts (check 11).
ledger.error_reason_convention: An ERROR is always accompanied by an error_reason on its layer record and a specific reason in run-metadata.txt. A status is never left unexplained.

3a.name: Sink and mitigation inventory
3a.criterion: all four inventories exist, both primary inventories are non-empty, all 19 sink and all 9 mitigation categories are covered, and every line matches the mandated format

evidence.test_partition_note: Verification check 6 requires only that the two test inventories exist. The 19-sink and 9-mitigation coverage obligation is asserted over the primary partition, so a category unrepresented in a test partition is not a defect.

path_safety.why_this_criterion_exists: The mandated row format <file>:<line>:<category>:<text> carries no escaping mechanism, so a path containing a colon or a control byte would make a row ambiguous rather than merely ugly: a crafted path such as evil:1:19:.ts occupies the file, line and category positions of the parse and displaces the real values, and the resulting row is still format-valid. Format validity alone therefore does not establish that a row means what it appears to mean, and the earlier wording of this record treated the format as unambiguous without stating the precondition that makes it so.
path_safety.precondition: every path emitted into any of the four inventories must be free of the colon delimiter, carriage return, line feed, NUL and every other control byte in the ranges 0x00-0x1F and 0x7F
path_safety.enforcement: Fail closed. If any path violates the precondition, Layer 3a is ERROR, the inventories are not accepted as a basis for Layer 3b, and the gate's ERROR branch fires and outranks BLOCK, WARN and PASS. The precondition is never waived, the offending row is never silently dropped, and the row is never re-encoded to make it parse.
path_safety.parse_rule: split on the first three colons only, so the text field retains every colon it legitimately contains - a CSP header value and a cookie attribute assignment both do
path_safety.consumer_side_guard: Independently of the precondition, every parsed path must resolve to a real file under the repository root. This is the guard that catches a mangled parse whose resulting path is itself free of delimiters, which is exactly the shape a spoofed row produces.
path_safety.conclusion: For this tree the precondition holds with zero exceptions, so the first-three-colon parse is unambiguous for every row and each parsed path round-trips to a real file. The precondition and its fail-closed rule are recorded as a standing requirement because they are what make that conclusion checkable; they are not a property of the row format itself.
path_safety.enforced_by: security-audit/verify.sh checks 4 and 16, which apply both the precondition and the on-disk round-trip guard and fail the check rather than warning

trust_boundary.claim_this_file_supports: Internal consistency of the audit artifact set at the revision named in provenance.audited_source_revision: that every attested output still hashes to its recorded digest, that every status is backed by a criterion this file states, and that the ledger and the merged summary agree with zero drift.
trust_boundary.claim_this_file_does_not_support: Authenticity, or integrity against tampering. This ledger, the digests it attests, the artifacts it describes and the harness that re-measures them all live in the same mutable checkout on the same branch. Anyone able to rewrite an artifact is equally able to rewrite its recorded digest, this ledger, the merged report and the harness, and the rewritten set would still verify clean. A self-attestation establishes consistency; it is not evidence of provenance.
trust_boundary.consequence_for_check_15: Check 15 re-measuring all attested digests and finding zero mismatch is necessary but not sufficient, and its PASS line says so in those terms rather than presenting the re-measurement as proof of authenticity.
requirements_on_a_consuming_gate: Regenerate the artifact set in a trusted context that the branch under review cannot write to, from the source revision named in provenance.audited_source_revision, and compare the result against the attested manifest. An artifact set supplied by the branch under review is evidence of nothing on its own.

Bind the comparison to that revision. If the tree being gated is not the revision the manifest was measured against, the comparison is meaningless and the affected layer status resolves to ERROR rather than being carried forward.

Obtain the digests over a channel the branch cannot write - a signed attestation, a provenance statement emitted by the build platform, or an artifact store keyed to the producing job - rather than reading them from this file.

Treat any mismatch between an externally attested digest and the value recorded here as ERROR, which outranks BLOCK, WARN and PASS in strict precedence, and never as a finding to be triaged or a warning to be noted.
trust_boundary.scope_of_this_work: This audit is read-only and adds no pipeline wiring, so the requirement is stated normatively here rather than implemented. Implementing it means changing CI, which the plan places outside this work.
trust_boundary.residual_risk: Until an external attestation exists, every status, digest and verdict in this artifact set is trustworthy exactly to the degree that the branch it sits on is trustworthy, and no further.

provenance.audited_source_revision_note: The codebase state every layer measured. Deliberately not the current branch tip, which advances with each artifact commit and is never a measurement basis.
provenance.run_id_basis: sha256 over the newline-terminated listing of every attested output as "<relative path> <sha256>", one per line, sorted by path, then hex-encoded. Reproduce it by rebuilding that listing from attested_outputs and hashing it; it is content-derived, so it is identical for identical outputs and changes the moment any attested byte changes.
provenance.attested_scope: The seventeen upstream artifacts whose existence and content these statuses assert. Deliberately excluded: layer-status.json itself (a file cannot carry its own digest), baseline.json and findings-merged.json (downstream consumers of this ledger - binding them here would invert the dependency direction), and run-metadata.txt (provenance narrative, not a layer output).
provenance.consumer_contract: A consumer MUST re-measure every attested output and compare bytes and sha256 before trusting any status here, and MUST verify audited_source_revision against the revision it is assessing. A missing artifact, a byte or digest mismatch, an absent status key, a status outside {OK, ERROR}, or a disagreement between a *_status key and its short-form twin resolves to ERROR - never to OK, and never by defaulting. The ERROR branch of the gate then fires and outranks BLOCK, WARN and PASS. This closes the failure mode in which a stale or forged all-OK ledger is paired with stale layer artifacts to suppress the ERROR branch.
provenance.binding_measured_at: immediately after the final write of every attested output and before the baseline and merged report were regenerated, so the digests describe the published bytes.
